official.title: Doctoral Researcher, Textile Chemistry
official.description_text:
Aalto University is where science and art meet technology and business. We shape a sustainable future by making research breakthroughs in and across our disciplines, sparking the game changers of tomorrow and creating novel solutions to major global challenges. Our community is made up of 16 000 students and 5 200 employees, including nearly 450 professors. Our campus is in Espoo, Greater Helsinki, Finland.  Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community.
The School of Chemical Engineering is one of the six schools of Aalto University. It combines natural sciences and engineering in a unique way.
The Textile Chemistry group is now looking for a
Doctoral Researcher in Textile Chemistry
The Textile Chemistry group (
https://www.aalto.fi/en/department-of-bioproducts-and-biosystems/textile-chemistry
) focuses on environmentally friendly textile coloration and post-treatment, textile recycling, and eTextiles.
We are now looking for a Doctoral Researcher to develop bio-based colorants from forest industry residues for textile dyeing and printing.
The research will be carried out in the
Department of Bioproducts and Biosystems
in the School of Chemical Engineering at Aalto University, in close collaboration with national and international research partners.
About the research
In this project, colorants will be extracted from materials such as bark and needles and evaluated in cotton dyeing and screen printing. Tannin-rich fractions will be tested as bio-based aids for color fixation. Laccase treatment will be tested as a way to improve color formation or retention. Washing, light exposure, and rubbing tests will show which approaches produce durable color. The research is planned in collaboration with the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke). The doctoral research will be done as a part of Aalto University Bioinnovation Center’s Doctoral School.
The research work includes
Extract, characterize, and standardize colorants from selected forest industry residues, accounting for variation between batches.
Design cotton dyeing experiments to assess how extract composition and fixation treatments affect color strength, shade consistency, and retention.
Develop cotton screen-printing pastes and evaluate color yield, print definition, and fixation.
Compare selected laccase treatments with appropriate controls and use chemical analyses to distinguish polymerization from aggregation.
Measure washing, light, and rubbing fastness of dyed and printed cotton and investigate colorant release and degradation.
Publish research findings, present results, and complete doctoral studies and a thesis.
Requirements
A relevant master’s degree, preferably in
biochemistry
or
textile chemistry
. Applicants with degrees in applied chemistry, chemical engineering, biotechnology, or related fields are also welcome.
A strong academic record and an interest in plant-derived colorants and textile coloration.
Hands-on laboratory experience, demonstrated through a master’s thesis or equivalent research, and the ability to design controlled experiments and interpret quantitative data.
The ability to work independently, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate research clearly in English.
Excellent verbal and written English communication skills
Experience with textile dyeing, printing, or colorfastness testing is particularly relevant for candidates with a textile chemistry background. For candidates with a biochemistry background, experience with enzyme assays, enzyme-catalyzed reactions, or phenolic compounds is especially valuable. Plant extraction, chromatography, spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry are also relevant.
What we offer
We offer a fixed-term contract initially for two years. During the first 6 months, you must apply for and receive the right to study in the doctoral programme in Chemical Engineering. After a successful evaluation by the end of the first 2-year contract, the contract can be extended. Extension of the contract is typically based on the progress evaluation, revised project plan and available funding. Funding for the position is secured from
BioInnovation center
.
The starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is about 3140 €/month (gross).
We work at the Otaniemi campus in Espoo, a vibrant and international research environment with excellent public transport connections, modern laboratory facilities, and a strong interdisciplinary academic community.
The preferred starting date is as soon as possible.
As a Doctoral Researcher, you will participate in doctoral courses, conduct high-quality scientific research under supervision, and may take part in teaching activities. You will be responsible for communicating your research results in meetings, project reports, and scientific conferences.
For more information
For additional information about the position, please contact Prof. Ali Tehrani, or in questions related to applying for the position, please contact HR Partner Noora Katisko (
firstname.lastname@aalto.fi
).
Ready to apply?
Follow the instructions carefully and submit a single pdf document (max. 10 pages in English) through the “Apply” link (not by email)
no later than December 15, 2026.
If you are an Aalto employee, you should apply for the position via our internal HR system Workday (Internal Jobs) by using your existing Workday user account (not via the external webpage for open positions).
To apply, please include the following documents in English and as a single pdf document:
Motivation letter specific to this project and description of previous relevant research experience (1 page)
CV with a possible list of publications and the title of your MSc thesis
Master’s degree certificate and overall GPA
English proficiency proof (Not needed for Aalto graduates)
List of 2-3 potential references with their emails
Important Note
:  Only candidates with a very good MSc GPA and documented proof of English proficiency will be considered for interview.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in textile chemistry focused on bio-based colorant extraction from forest residues, dyeing experiments, and durability testing. Research is laboratory-intensive with emphasis on chemical characterization, experimental design, and synthesis.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. The position is rooted in chemistry, materials science, and textile engineering. The researcher's identity is human-centred XR, immersive learning, and spatial cognition. No connection exists between forest-derived colorants and immersive systems or human factors research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Limited methodological alignment. The researcher has experimental-design and quantitative-research skills applicable to any empirical work. However, textile chemistry requires domain-specific laboratory protocols, chemical analysis, and synthesis techniques entirely outside the researcher's demonstrated expertise (which is software development, XR design, and user studies). The experimental contexts are fundamentally different.

growth_value.rationale: Minimal growth value toward the target identity. This position would require learning chemistry and materials science from scratch, moving the researcher away from human-centred research, collaborative systems, and immersive design. It does not close any gaps relevant to XR/HCI or spatial-learning research.

strategic_value.rationale: Aalto University is a strong institution in target geography (Finland) with excellent funding stability and research environment. However, textile chemistry is an isolated domain within chemical engineering. Supervisory quality and institutional prestige cannot offset the fundamental mismatch in research direction.

eligibility_flags: Posting requires 'relevant master's degree, preferably in biochemistry or textile chemistry.' Researcher holds MSc by Research in multimedia/HCI — domain is not chemistry. Eligibility uncertain.
Posting states 'hands-on laboratory experience, demonstrated through a master's thesis' — researcher's thesis is in XR application design, not chemistry.
risks: Complete domain mismatch: moving from software/XR into chemistry would represent a career pivot, not a natural progression.
No transferable technical expertise in laboratory protocols, chemical synthesis, spectroscopy, or colorimetry.
Research community and publication venues entirely different; network effects diminished.
May not meet selection criteria given chemistry background requirement and lack of textile/chemical laboratory evidence.
